question: Can I claim a vendor paid dinner?

candidate_answer.answer: Vendors may host events involving dinners, and accepting vendor-sponsored meals must comply with both the Travel & Expense Policy and the Code of Business Conduct [S2]. All invoices, receipts, or sponsorship acknowledgements should be recorded to avoid conflicts of interest and ensure proper reconciliation [S2]. High-value vendor engagements may require Finance, Compliance, and Procurement sign-offs [S2]. Please note that the specific reimbursement limit for the dinner depends on whether it falls within standard daily meal caps (such as the USD 45 dinner limit) [S4] or involves other specific claim conditions, which are unspecified.

Code of Business Conduct & Ethics
Policy ID: LEG-ETH-001
Version: 5.1
Effective Date: 1 January 2025
Statement from Leadership
Apex Global’s reputation is built on ethical conduct and personal accountability.

This Code
outlines the principles that guide our decisions and actions across all markets in which we
operate.

1.

Gifts & Entertainment
• Gifts over USD 100 must be disclosed.

• Gifts over USD 250 are prohibited.

• Client-hosted dinners or entertainment may be accepted but must be reported in
conjunction with Finance policies to ensure reimbursement limits and conflicts of
interest are observed.

Employees should consult both the Code of Business Conduct and the Travel & Expense
Policy when submitting claims for client-hosted meals or entertainment.

Scenarios
include:
• Client Dinner: If the client pays for a dinner exceeding the standard USD 45 limit,
employees must still record and disclose it.

• Alcohol at Client Events: Alcohol can be consumed at client-hosted events but
reimbursement requires disclosure.

• Multiple Approvals: Some high-value client dinners may require both Finance and
Compliance approval.

Employees must ensure that accepting such benefits does not create a conflict of interest,
in line with corporate ethics standards.

3.

Conflicts of Interest
Employees must disclose any personal or financial interests that could influence business
decisions.

This includes accepting meals, gifts, or reimbursements that may affect
decision-making.

Workplace & Flexible Work Policy
Policy ID: HR-WRK-012
Version: 3.0
Effective Date: 1 March 2025
Owner: Human Resources

Policy Intent
Apex Global is committed to providing a productive, safe, and flexible workplace
environment that supports both on-site and remote employees. This policy consolidates
prior remote work, office attendance, and workplace support guidelines into a single
framework intended to promote consistency, employee well-being, and operational
effectiveness.
This policy replaces earlier standalone Remote & Hybrid Work policies unless otherwise
stated.

1. Scope
This policy applies to all regular full-time and part-time employees of Apex Global. Certain
roles may be subject to additional workplace requirements due to regulatory, operational,
or security considerations.

2. Workplace Models
• On-site: Employees work primarily from an Apex Global office location.
• Hybrid: Employees split time between an Apex Global office and a remote location.
• Remote: Employees work primarily from a remote location approved by their
manager and HR.

3. Eligibility & Approval
• Employees must have a minimum of 6 months of service to be eligible for hybrid or
remote arrangements.
• Participation is subject to manager approval and periodic review.

Global Travel & Expense Reimbursement Policy
Policy ID: FIN-T&E-001
Version: 3.2
Effective Date: 1 January 2025
Last Reviewed: 15 December 2024
Owner: Finance Operations

Executive Overview
At Apex Global, business travel plays a critical role in supporting client relationships,
cross-regional collaboration, and strategic growth initiatives. This policy reflects Apex
Global’s commitment to balancing employee flexibility with prudent financial stewardship.
All employees are expected to exercise sound judgment and align travel decisions with the
firm’s values of integrity, accountability, and operational excellence.
This document supersedes prior versions unless explicitly stated otherwise. Employees
are responsible for familiarizing themselves with the contents of this policy prior to
incurring any travel-related expenses.

1. Purpose
This policy establishes guidelines for reimbursable travel and business expenses incurred
by Apex Global employees to ensure fiscal responsibility, regulatory compliance, and fair
treatment across regions.

2. Scope
This policy applies to all full-time employees, part-time employees, and long-term
contractors traveling on behalf of Apex Global.

3. General Reimbursement Principles
• Expenses must be business-related, reasonable, and necessary.
• Itemized receipts are required for all expenses above USD 25.
• Expenses must be submitted within 30 days of travel completion.
• Expenses submitted after 60 days may be denied without exception.

sources.text: explicitly stated otherwise. Employees are responsible for familiarizing themselves with the contents of this policy prior to incurring any travel-related expenses. 1. Purpose This policy establishes guidelines for reimbursable travel and business expenses incurred by Apex Global employees to ensure fiscal responsibility, regulatory compliance, and fair treatment across regions. 2. Scope This policy applies to all full-time employees, part-time employees, and long-term contractors traveling on behalf of Apex Global. 3. General Reimbursement Principles • Expenses must be business-related, reasonable, and necessary. • Itemized receipts are required for all expenses above USD 25. • Expenses must be submitted within 30 days of travel completion. • Expenses submitted after 60 days may be denied without exception.

sources.text: 4. Booking & Travel Approval Apex Global seeks to standardize travel booking to improve duty-of-care, negotiate preferred rates, and ensure compliance with local regulations. • Domestic travel requires people-manager approval. • International travel requires Director-level approval. • Employees are encouraged, but not required, to use the Apex Global Travel Portal. 5. Lodging Limits Region Maximum Reimbursement North America USD 275 Europe EUR 240 Asia-Pacific USD 200 5.1 High-Cost City Exception For designated high-cost cities (Tokyo, Singapore, Hong Kong, Zurich): - Asia-Pacific cap may increase to USD 230 - Requires pre-trip Finance approval
